svg.title: Family scaling profile by benchmark
svg.desc: Five-panel family view across all benchmark lines. The top row plots only trustworthy comparable accuracy for UniMoral, SMID, and Value Kaleidoscope. The bottom row shows CCD-Bench and Denevil as status-curve panels so all five benchmarks appear as chart panels while preserving the non-comparable coverage meaning of those benchmarks.
svg.text: Five benchmark panels: three scored accuracy charts plus two coverage-status charts.
Top row: scored benchmarks only (`UniMoral`, `SMID`, `Value Kaleidoscope`).
Bottom row: `CCD-Bench` and `Denevil` are shown as status curves
because the public package tracks completion / proxy coverage there rather than one shared accuracy scalar.
Missing top-row points are evidence limits or withheld accuracy cells, not zeroes.
Dashed connectors skip missing size slots; no point means no public comparable score.
Average of moral rating and foundation classification
Dashed connectors skip missing size slots; no point means no public comparable score.
Average of relevance and valence accuracy
Dashed connectors skip missing size slots; no point means no public comparable score.
Higher bands mean more complete public coverage, not higher accuracy.
Top band means proxy-complete coverage, not benchmark-faithful accuracy.
Panels 4-5 are status curves, not accuracy curves.
Higher bands mean more complete publication state,
and family traces are slightly offset for readability.
DeepSeek-M stays out of the top-row accuracy panels because
its saved short-answer rerun still shows 100.0% empty visible answers.
Qwen: text scored at S/M/L; SMID has S/L.
DeepSeek: only L is scored up top; bottom status curves still show M.
Llama: text scored at S/M/L; SMID has S/L.
All five benchmarks now appear as chart panels.
Bottom status curves keep `CCD-Bench` and `Denevil` visible
without implying a shared directly comparable accuracy scalar.
Takeaway: current evidence supports task-specific scaling statements, not a single universal size law across all families and benchmarks.
